findings.current: 此地址不是私有地址——此手机与它之间的任何一方都能读取密码。
findings.problem: “此手机与它之间的任何一方” is not idiomatic: “任何一方” evokes “either party” (of the phone and the address), so the warning about anything on the path in between can be misread and is weakened; “它” is also vague. The note asks for a strong warning.
findings.suggested: 此地址不是私有地址——从此手机到该地址途经的任何网络或设备都能读取密码。

findings.problem: “公开电脑” (publicise/disclose the computer) is an unusual collocation for “expose”; the body under it says 暴露到互联网上 and the URL label uses 公网. Understandable, but the heading and body use different terms.
findings.suggested: 将电脑暴露到公网前须知

findings.current: 使用http://时，中继密码会以明文在网络中传输，因此默认关闭，需你手动开启。只要地址支持，请始终使用https://。
findings.problem: “需你手动开启” can be read as “you need to turn it on”, which nudges toward the unsafe option. The English says it stays off unless you turn it on.
findings.suggested: 使用http://时，中继密码会以明文在网络中传输，因此除非你手动开启，否则此选项保持关闭。只要地址支持，请始终使用https://。

findings.current: 在保存任何内容之前，这会先通过你的隧道发送一次真实请求。
findings.problem: The subject “这会先” is a calque of “This makes”. Chinese drops it.
findings.suggested: 保存前，会先通过你的隧道发送一次真实请求。

findings.current: 此地址位于你自己的网络内，因此风险仅限于该网络。
findings.problem: “风险” generalises “exposure”. “暴露范围” is more exact and matches the security body.
findings.suggested: 此地址位于你自己的网络内，因此暴露范围仅限于该网络。

per_key_results.english: You are putting your own computer on the internet, and the relay password is the only thing standing in front of it. Prefer HTTPS, use a tunnel that offers its own authentication where yours does, and rotate the password with `{command}` if it has been shared. Anyone with that password and your URL can drive the sessions on that machine.
